en: Netti:
The Section on Exposition of the Counter-Demonstrations (Paṭiniddesavāra Vibhaṅga) 9
The Analysis of the Mode of Conveying Reversal.
Therein, what is the mode of conveying reversal?
It is: "Wholesome and unwholesome states."
For a person of right view, wrong view is worn away.
Whatever numerous evil, unwholesome states might arise conditioned by wrong view are worn away for him.
Conditioned by right view, numerous wholesome states arise for him, and these reach fulfillment through development.
For a person of right intention, wrong intention is worn away.
Whatever numerous evil, unwholesome states might arise conditioned by wrong intention are worn away for such a person.
And conditioned by right intention, numerous wholesome states come to be.
And these reach fulfillment through cultivation.
Thus, for a person who possesses right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right liberation,
and right knowledge and vision of liberation, wrong knowledge and vision of liberation is worn away.
Whatever numerous evil, unwholesome states might arise in him conditioned by wrong liberation through knowledge and vision have been worn away by him.
Conditioned by right liberation through knowledge and vision, numerous wholesome states arise in him, and they reach fulfillment through development.
Or, for one who abstains from the destruction of life, the destruction of life has been abandoned.
For one who abstains from taking what is not given, taking what is not given is abandoned.
For one who lives the holy life, unchastity is abandoned.
For one who speaks the truth, false speech is abandoned.
For one who speaks without divisiveness, divisive speech has been abandoned.
For one who speaks gently, harsh speech has been abandoned.
For one who speaks at the proper time, idle chatter has been abandoned.
In one who is free from covetousness, covetousness has been abandoned.
In one whose mind is free from ill will, ill will has been abandoned.
In one with right view, wrong view has been abandoned.
But as for those who disparage the Noble Eightfold Path, they incur legitimate and visible censure and reproach according to the Dhamma.
Since you, sirs, disparage the Dhamma of right view,
by that very fact you are to be honored and praised by those who hold wrong views.

In this way, those venerable ones criticize the Dhamma of right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right liberation, and right knowledge and vision of liberation.
Therefore, those who possess wrong liberation and wrong knowledge and vision of liberation are the ones whom you venerable ones should honor and praise.

And as for those who say: "Sensual pleasures should be enjoyed, sensual pleasures should be partaken of, sensual pleasures should be cultivated, sensual pleasures should be indulged in, sensual pleasures should be developed, sensual pleasures should be practiced extensively."
Abstaining from sensual pleasures is non-Dhamma for them.
Or, as for those who say, "Devotion to self-mortification is Dhamma," for them,
that which leads to liberation is non-Dhamma.
And as for those who say, "The Dhamma is suffering," for them the Dhamma is non-Dhamma. Or rather,
just as for a bhikkhu dwelling contemplating foulness in all conditioned formations, perceptions of beauty are abandoned.
For one who dwells contemplating suffering, perceptions of pleasure are abandoned.
For one who dwells contemplating impermanence, perceptions of permanence are abandoned.
For one who dwells contemplating non-self, perceptions of self are abandoned.
Furthermore, whatever state one finds agreeable or approaches, the opposite of that state becomes undesirable and is thereby encountered.
Therefore the Venerable Mahākaccāyana said: "Wholesome and unwholesome states.
The Mode of Conveying Reversal is concluded.
